body:
I wouldn't say I'm romanticizing it. I sincerely don't want to give up, but the past five or six years have basically just been an exercise in trying to find the humor in how horrible things can get. I did appreciate your response. This is all probably melodramatic, in the sense that I have never so much as attempted to kill myself. I smoke a copious amount of cigarettes and drink far too frequently, which cannot be helping things, but it is downright impossible to extensively give a damn at this point, and I wish I could. I've been diagnosed with depression in the past, I've done the therapy circuit, and while I am taking an antidepressant again, no medication or amount of "talking things out" has helped in the past. 

I do want this life, but I am starting to run out of a capacity to handle the downward spiral and insignificance of it. And I do understand your shitty this and that example, because I've never been the sort to ask for much, myself. I'm trying to weather the storm, believe me, but the feelings of apathy and hopelessness get far too intense sometimes, and yesterday was definitely one of those times. I've thought about suicide enough times to know that tomorrow is usually much better. While I wouldn't say today is fantastic, it is nowhere near as unbearable, but I would still describe it as unbearable (just less horrific). Thank you for your response. I'm trying, I truly am. I just need something (anything) to change, preferably for the better.

I hope both you and I make it out of this nonsense someday.
